rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The denier likened God to created beings unable to revive decayed bones, forgetting that God first created him.
rows.anchor: لا يعجز أن يعيد الأموات أحياء، والعظام الرميم بشرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man forgot God made him from a drop into a complete, articulate human; the Creator who originated him can restore the dead to their former form.
rows.anchor: من خلقه من نطفة حتى صار بشرا سويا ناطقا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one who revives the bones is the one who first brought them into being when they were nothing.
rows.anchor: يحييها الذي ابتدع خلقها أول مرة ولم تكن شيئا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God knows every creature and how to cause death, revive, originate, and restore; nothing about His creation is hidden.
rows.anchor: وهو بجميع خلقه ذو علم كيف يميت، وكيف يحيي،

words: أوليس الذي خلق السموات والأرض بقادر
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse rebukes the denier's ignorance: the Creator of the seven heavens and earth can create people like them.
rows.anchor: بأعظم من خلق السموات والأرض يقول: فمن لم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Since creating the heavens and earth is greater than creating humans, the One who did the greater act can readily revive decayed bones.
rows.anchor: فمن لم يتعذر عليه خلق ما هو أعظم من خلقكم،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh chiefs urged people to proceed in their religion and persist in worshipping their gods.
rows.anchor: انطلقوا مشيا ومضيا على دينكم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The particle أن is accusative in place and attached to انطلقوا, meaning to set out walking and proceeding.
rows.anchor: في موضع نصب يتعلق انطلقوا بها

rows.speaker: عبد الله
rows.claim: A reading attributed to Abdullah has the chiefs setting out while walking and saying to persevere with their gods.
rows.anchor: قراءة عبد الله: «وانطلق الملأ منهم يمشون

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid identifies the speaker who set out as ʿUqbah ibn Abī Muʿayṭ.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد: {وانطلق الملأ منهم} [ص: 6]

words: ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas identifies the latter religion as Christianity; the reported view says Quraysh had not heard Muhammad's call to worship God alone or his scripture in that faith.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة} [ص: 7] يقول: «النصرانية»

words: ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة
rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says they argued that if the Quran were true, Christians would have told them about it.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة

rows.speaker: القرظي
rows.claim: Al-Quraẓī glosses the latter religion as the religion of Jesus.
rows.anchor: عن القرظي في قوله: {ما سمعنا بهذا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī also identifies the latter religion as Christianity.
rows.anchor: عن السدي {ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Another view from Mujahid takes it to mean that they had not heard this in the Quraysh religion.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، في قوله: {ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada understands it as their own religion and their own time: they had never heard this in their religion or era.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {ما سمعنا بهذا في الملة الآخرة}

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says الآخرة means the other or later religion, while milla means religion.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ما سمعنا بهذا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: It is also said that those who set out were Quraysh elders, including Abu Jahl, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, and al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth.
rows.anchor: وقيل: إن الملأ الذين انطلقوا نفر من مشيخة قريش

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī recounts Quraysh elders—Abu Jahl, al-ʿĀṣ ibn Wāʾil, al-Aswad ibn al-Muṭṭalib, and al-Aswad ibn ʿAbd Yaghūth—meeting to ask Abu Talib to stop Muhammad's criticism of their gods and leave each side to its worship; they feared Arab reproach if they attacked after his death.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، أن أناسا من قريش اجتمعوا، فيهم أبو جهل

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: In al-Suddī's account, Muhammad told Abu Talib he called Quraysh to a word by which Arabs would submit and they would rule the non-Arabs; when he said “There is no god but God,” they rejected alternatives, left angrily, and threatened him.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، أن أناسا من قريش اجتمعوا، فيهم

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: At Abu Talib's deathbed, Muhammad urged him to profess that there is no god but God; Abu Talib declined lest Arabs say he feared death, and stayed with his forefathers' religion.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، أن أناسا من قريش اجتمعوا

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī's account says that after Abu Talib refused the profession of faith, the verse “You do not guide whom you love” (28:56) was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، أن أناسا من قريش اجتمعوا

words: وانطلق الملأ منهم أن امشوا واصبروا على آلهتكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭabarī reports from Ibn Abbas that the verse about Quraysh's chiefs setting out was revealed when they went to Abu Talib to discuss the Prophet.
rows.anchor: نزلت حين انطلق أشراف قريش إلى أبي طالب فكلموه في النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quraysh claim that the Quran is اختلاق means it is a lie Muhammad fabricated and made up.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، {إن هذا إلا اختلاق} [ص: 7] «اختلقه محمد صلى الله عليه وسلم»

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas glosses اختلاق as false conjecture or fabrication.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {إن هذا إلا اختلاق}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses اختلاق as a lie.
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، في قوله: {إن هذا إلا اختلاق}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says it is something they make up.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {إن هذا إلا اختلاق}

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says it is something Muhammad fabricated.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، {إن هذا إلا اختلاق}

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says their claim means that this is only a lie.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {إن هذا إلا اختلاق}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person whose heart God expands for Islam knows Him, affirms His oneness and lordship, submits to obedience, and gains insight and certainty through truth's illumination.
rows.anchor: فهو على بصيرة مما هو عليه ويقين، بتنوير الحق في قلبه، فهو لذلك لأمر الله متبع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The comparison's other half and the interrogative's answer are left implicit for listeners to infer; the warning about hardened hearts supplies the contrast.
rows.anchor: وجواب الاستفهام اجتزاء بمعرفة السامعين المراد من الكلام، إذ ذكر

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada identifies the light as God's Book, which the believer believes, takes, and follows.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī explains that God has made the person's chest spacious for Islam.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {أفمن شرح الله صدره

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the light as guidance.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، قوله: {أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام}

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the one whose breast is open to Islam is unlike the one whose heart is hardened.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، {أفمن شرح الله صدره للإسلام}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hardened hearts are dry, distant from God's remembrance, and turned away from the Quran He sent as a reminder; their owners do not believe or affirm its contents.
rows.anchor: كما يقال في الكلام: أتخمت من طعام أكلته، وعن طعام أكلته بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here من means عن; Arabic can use either preposition in expressions such as being made ill from food one ate.
rows.anchor: أتخمت من طعام أكلته، وعن طعام أكلته بمعنى واحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The best discourse God sent down is the Quran.
rows.anchor: الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran's parts resemble one another, with no disagreement or contradiction.
rows.anchor: يشبه بعضه بعضا، لا اختلاف فيه، ولا تضاد

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says each verse resembles another verse and each letter resembles another letter.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {الله نزل أحسن الحديث

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī glosses the description as parts of the Book resembling one another.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، {كتابا متشابها} [الزمر: 23] قال

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Saʿīd ibn Jubayr says the Quran's parts resemble, confirm, and point to one another.
rows.anchor: عن سعيد بن جبير، في قوله: {كتابا متشابها}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Quran repeats accounts, reports, judgments, legal rulings, and proofs within it.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {مثاني} [الزمر: 23] قال: «ثنى الله فيه الفرائض، والقضاء، والحدود»

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan says God repeated judgments in the Book, with a verse in one surah resembling a verse in another.
rows.anchor: عن الحسن، في قوله: {الله نزل أحسن الحديث كتابا

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid says the Quran throughout is described as recurring pairs.
rows.anchor: عن مجاهد، قوله: {كتابا متشابها مثاني}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says obligations, judgments, and prescribed penalties are repeated in the Quran.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {مثاني} [الزمر: 23] قال

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas says the Book repeats a matter many times.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قوله: {مثاني} [الزمر: 23] قال

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī says the Book repeats matters many times and in more than one place.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، في قوله: {مثاني} [الزمر: 23] قال

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd says the Quran repeats material, recounting Moses, Salih, Hud, and other prophets in many places.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد في قوله: {مثاني} [الزمر: 23]

words: تقشعر منه جلود الذين يخشون ربهم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When the God-fearing hear the Quran recited, their skins shiver; then their skins and hearts soften toward God's remembrance, meaning acting on and affirming the Book.
rows.anchor: تقشعر من سماعه إذا تلي عليهم جلود الذين يخافون ربهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that when the Companions asked the Prophet to tell them stories, this verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس، قالوا: يا رسول الله لو حدثتنا؟

rows.speaker: عمرو بن قيس
rows.claim: A report from ʿAmr ibn Qays likewise says people asked the Prophet for a narration and this verse followed.
rows.anchor: عن عمرو بن قيس، قال: قالوا: يا نبي الله،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The shivering and subsequent softening described are God's guidance and enabling of those people.
rows.anchor: هذا الذي يصيب هؤلاء القوم الذين وصفت صفتهم عند سماعهم القرآن من اقشعرار جلودهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God guides whichever servants He wills by means of the Quran.
rows.anchor: يهدي تبارك وتعالى بالقرآن من يشاء من عباده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, “that” may refer to the Quran itself: it is God's clarification, by which He guides whom He wills to believe in it.
rows.anchor: وقد يتوجه معنى قوله: {ذلك هدى} [الزمر: 23]

words: ومن يضلل الله فما له من هاد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Whoever God leaves astray from belief in and affirmation of the Quran has no guide to enable or direct him to follow it.
rows.anchor: ومن يخذله الله عن الإيمان بهذا القرآن والتصديق بما فيه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The polytheists threaten Muhammad with their idols, claiming they will harm him for rejecting and criticizing them; God will suffice him.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada recounts that Muhammad sent Khalid ibn al-Walid to smash al-ʿUzza; its keeper warned him, but Khalid struck the idol's nose with an axe.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه}

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddī identifies those invoked besides God as the gods Quraysh worshipped.
rows.anchor: عن السدي، {ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه}

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: Ibn Zayd likewise says they threatened Muhammad with the gods worshipped besides God.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد، في قوله: {ويخوفونك بالذين من دونه}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: When distress strikes, a person calls on God for help; after God relieves it with ease, wealth, health, and well-being, the person claims the favor came through his own knowledge and merit.
rows.anchor: فإذا أصاب الإنسان بؤس وشدة دعانا مستغيثا بنا من جهة ما أصابه من الضر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The person claims he received prosperity because God knew he deserved it through his distinction and approved deeds; عندي means in my own estimation.
rows.anchor: يعني على علم من الله بأني له أهل لشرفي

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid glosses خولناه as “We gave him.”
rows.anchor: عن ابن أبي نجيح، عن مجاهد، قوله: {إذا خولناه نعمة منا}

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada understands the claim as meaning that the favor came because of good standing in the recipient's own estimation.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ثم إذا خولناه نعمة منا}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The favor given after distress is a trial and test for the people who receive it.
rows.anchor: بل عطيتنا إياهم تلك النعمة من بعد الضر الذي كانوا فيه فتنة لهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Most people fail to understand why they received the favor because of ignorance and poor judgment.
rows.anchor: {لا يعلمون} [البقرة: 13] لأي سبب أعطوا ذلك

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses فتنة here as a trial or affliction.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة {بل هي فتنة} [الزمر: 49] : «أي بلاء»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God will repay every soul for good and evil deeds; He knows all obedience and disobedience, nothing escapes His knowledge, and He will reward the good and requite the evil on Judgment Day.
rows.anchor: وفى الله حينئذ كل نفس جزاء عملها من خير وشر،

words: وسيق الذين كفروا إلى جهنم زمرا
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers are gathered and driven to the fire prepared for them on Judgment Day in successive groups and parties.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {زمرا} [الزمر: 71] قال: «جماعات»

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses زمرا as groups.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، في قوله: {زمرا} [الزمر: 71] قال: «جماعات»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Hell has seven opened gates; its keepers, the custodians, question the disbelievers.
rows.anchor: قال الذين كفروا مجيبين لخزنة جهنم

words: ألم يأتكم رسل منكم يتلون عليكم آيات ربكم
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keepers ask whether messengers from among the disbelievers recited God's revealed Book and proofs sent to their peoples.
rows.anchor: فأنذرتنا لقاءنا هذا اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The messengers warned them about what they would meet that day.
rows.anchor: فأنذرتنا لقاءنا هذا اليوم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternative explanation takes the warning to mean that they were warned about their destination on that day.
rows.anchor: أن يكون معناه: وينذرونكم مصيركم إلى هذا اليوم

words: قالوا بلى ولكن حقت كلمة العذاب على الكافرين
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The disbelievers admit messengers came from their own people and warned them, but say God's sentence of punishment became due because they disbelieved.
rows.anchor: قال الذين كفروا مجيبين لخزنة جهنم: بلى قد أتتنا الرسل منا،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says God's sentence of punishment became due because of their deeds.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، قوله: {ولكن حقت كلمة العذاب على الكافرين}

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh tells his court to let him kill Moses and let Moses call the Lord he claims sent him to protect him; Pharaoh says Moses will change their religion by his magic.
rows.anchor: يغير دينكم الذي أنتم عليه بسحره

rows.speaker: قراء المدينة والشام والبصرة
rows.claim: Most readers in Medina, Syria, and Basra read وأن without an alif, as in the Medinan codices.
rows.anchor: قرأ ذلك عامة قراء المدينة والشام والبصرة: (وأن يظهر في الأرض الفساد)

words: أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد
rows.speaker: قراء الكوفة
rows.claim: Most Kufan readers read أو أن with an alif, as in their codices, and read يظهر with a fatḥa on yāʾ and الفساد in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ذلك عامة قراء الكوفة: {أو أن} [هود: 87] بالألف،

words: أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Tabari accepts both widespread conjunction readings as close in meaning: whether corruption is made manifest or appears, an agent's manifestation is implicit.
rows.anchor: والصواب من القول في ذلك عندنا أنهما قراءتان مشهورتان

words: أخاف أن يبدل دينكم أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh feared Moses would change their religion or openly establish worship of his Lord in Egypt, which Pharaoh considered corruption; replacing their religion with its opposite amounted to making corruption appear.
rows.anchor: ففي القراءة بإحدى القراءتين في ذلك دليل واضح على صحة معنى الأخرى،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada glosses their religion as the affair or condition they currently follow.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {إني أخاف أن يبدل دينكم} [غافر: 26]

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says that for Pharaoh, corruption meant acting in obedience to God.
rows.anchor: عن قتادة، {إني أخاف أن يبدل دينكم} [غافر: 26] «أي أمركم الذي أنتم عليه» {أو أن يظهر في الأرض الفساد}

words: إني عذت بربي وربكم من كل متكبر لا يؤمن بيوم الحساب
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses seeks refuge in his and Pharaoh's Lord from every arrogant person who rejects God's oneness, divinity, and obedience and does not believe in the Day of Reckoning.
rows.anchor: استجرت أيها القوم بربي وربكم، من كل متكبر عليه،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses singled out people who deny reckoning because they neither hope for reward for good deeds nor fear punishment for evil; such people are the specific object of his plea for refuge.
rows.anchor: خص موسى صلوات الله وسلامه عليه، الاستعاذة بالله ممن لا يؤمن بيوم الحساب،
